subject: Re: GreenWave MSA — derivative access limits + data-use evidence
messages:
From: Eloise Chen <eloise.chen@greenwave.io>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: David Park <david.park@gw-legal.com>, procurement@greenwave.io
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GreenWave MSA redlines (attached)

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the run-through yesterday. Attached are our redlines to the MSA (see GreenWave_MSA_Redlines_v1.docx and a short summary). High level asks:

- We need a clear carveout that prevents Redwood from using any customer prompts, outputs, or logs for model retraining or to improve models that could be used in production for other customers.
- For derivative/"product" claims, GreenWave requests an explicit prohibition on redistribution of outputs that contain customer-provided confidential templates; we'd accept an export path for internal analytics only.
- Telemetry & usage: we will only permit anonymized, aggregated telemetry for platform health; anything that could identify request/response pairs tied to account IDs must be blocked.
- Evidence/evidence path: our procurement team needs a one-week window to review any proposed technical proof that telemetry is anonymized. Please provide a list of artifacts you can share (logs, data-flow diagram, redaction rules).

Can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to accept the retraining/derivative carveout as drafted? If not, please propose alternate language and the specific operational controls you will put in place. The procurement lead (cc'd) needs this by next Wednesday to keep the Q3 procurement cadence.

Best,
Eloise Chen
Contracts & Procurement
GreenWave Inc.

---
Attachments: GreenWave_MSA_Redlines_v1.docx, redline_summary_gw.pdf

Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GreenWave MSA redlines (attached)

Hi Eloise — thanks for the fast turnaround and for the clear summary. We reviewed the doc and have a few internal asks before proposing alternate language.

Quick notes:
- We understand GreenWave's need to limit retraining and derivative claims. Redwood's typical approach is to offer a contractual training prohibition plus an operational enforcement plan (separate opt-out flags, dedicated VPC modes, and no-feedback ingestion by default).
- For telemetry, we already offer an anonymized telemetry tier and can provide a data-flow diagram; we'll need to confirm the exact artifacts we can share given internal privacy constraints.
- For outputs that incorporate customer confidential templates, we think a scoped productization carveout (export allowed only in accounts with explicit consent and with attribution controls) will be acceptable on our side, but legal needs to align on the exact phrasing.

Looping in Ben (sales lead) and Laura/Markus (legal/ops) to draft suggested language and provide the evidence list Eloise requested. Ben — can you confirm commercial impact if GreenWave requires the training prohibition as-is? Laura/Markus — would appreciate proposed redline text and a short list of artifacts (ideally 3 items) we can share next week.

Talk soon —
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: RE: GW redlines — commercial and rollout notes

Laura / Markus — quick commercial context for legal: if GreenWave insists on a permanent blanket ban on any use of outputs or prompts for model improvement across all deployment modes, the likely commercial outcomes are:

- Hosted API (standard plan): material price uplift or inability to meet their feature needs (we rely on aggregated telemetry to maintain performance and fights fraud).
- Dedicated / Private (VPC or on-prem): feasible to meet strict non-training requirements with contractual and technical controls; this is where we can accept the strongest carveouts but there is higher cost.

Our suggested path: propose two tiers in the MSA language — (A) hosted: limited anonymized telemetry only, no customer-specific retraining; (B) private/dedicated: explicit non-training covenant with audit/evidence path and compensating credits. That keeps procurement flexible and aligns with product capabilities.

Can legal draft two short alternative clauses (<= 3 sentences each): one for hosted and one for dedicated/private. Also please include the artifact list Eloise asked for (data-flow diagram, telemetry sample with hashes redacted, and a one-page ops note on feedback ingestion controls).

Thanks — Ben

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Eloise Chen <eloise.chen@greenwave.io>, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GreenWave MSA redlines (attached) — proposed compromise language and artifacts

Eloise / Camila — attaching a brief redline excerpt (we returned the full tracked copy via Drive link) and an artifacts bundle. Summary below and proposed language for the MSA: 

Summary (plain English):
- Hosted service: Redwood will not use customer-provided prompts, outputs, or Content for model retraining. We will collect anonymized, aggregated telemetry for platform health and security that cannot be tied to account identifiers; we will share a one-page telemetry proof artifact for procurement to review.
- Dedicated/private deployments: customer may elect a strict non-training option (no telemetry collection beyond heartbeat/uptime). In that case we will offer a discounted dedicated plan and provide an on-site or Redacted Drive audit sample under NDA.
- Derivative/productization: we propose a limited export carveout — GreenWave may commercialize its own outputs and templates; Redwood will not surface GreenWave-specific prompts or outputs to other customers. If GreenWave requests cross-account productization assistance, that will be subject to a separate SOW.

Proposed short clause (hosted): "Redwood will not use Customer-provided prompts, outputs, or Content for model training or tuning of models that may be used to serve other customers. Redwood may collect and retain aggregated, anonymized telemetry for service health and security; such telemetry will not contain Customer account identifiers or verbatim prompt/response text. Redwood will provide a one-page telemetry proof artifact for Customer review upon request."

Proposed short clause (dedicated/private): "For Dedicated or Private deployments, Customer may elect a Non-Training Mode in which Redwood will not collect telemetry beyond service availability and will not use Customer Content for model training. If Customer elects Non-Training Mode, parties will document the configuration and any commercial adjustments in an Order Form or SOW."

Artifacts we can share now:
- redline_summary_gw.pdf (explains clause mapping)
- telemetry_dataflow.pdf (diagram of data collection and redaction points)
- telemetry_sample_hashed.csv (sample logs with account fields hashed)

If that addresses your procurement checklist we can hubspot-tag the deal and get procurement to confirm. Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow if helpful.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
